tickets.title: [Setup] Project setup (server + web + admin)
tickets.body:
**Side:** All · **Phase:** M1 Setup & Auth · **Priority:** High · **Type:** Setup

### Summary
Set up the base structure of all repos so every developer works the same way. This is a multi-tenant system: every shop owner gets one account and one `tenant_id`.

### What we'll use, and why
| Area | Tool | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| Backend | NestJS + TypeScript | API structure (modules, guards, services) |
| Database | PostgreSQL + Drizzle ORM + drizzle-kit | Data, type-safe queries, migrations |
| Backend config | @nestjs/config + Zod | Validated env variables |
| API docs | @nestjs/swagger | Auto docs at `/docs` |
| Security | helmet, CORS, @nestjs/throttler | Secure headers, allowed origins, rate limits |
| Logging | nestjs-pino | Request and error logs |
| Local dev | Docker Compose | Postgres (and later Redis) |
| Frontend | Next.js (App Router) + TypeScript | web and admin apps |
| UI | Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui | Components, theming, RTL later |
| Server state | TanStack Query | API data, caching |
| HTTP | Axios | Base instance + interceptors |
| Client state | Zustand | UI and session state |
| Forms | React Hook Form + Zod | Validation |
| Code quality | ESLint + Prettier + Husky + lint-staged | Same style, checks before each commit |
| Testing | Jest + supertest (server), Vitest + RTL, Playwright (frontend) | All test types |

### Tasks
- [ ] **server:** NestJS project, folder structure (`modules/`, `common/`, `database/`, `config/`)
- [ ] **server:** Docker Compose with Postgres, `.env.example`
- [ ] **server:** Drizzle setup, global `DatabaseModule`, first migration
- [ ] **server:** base tables `tenants` and `users` with `tenant_id`, timestamps, `deleted_at`
- [ ] **server:** Swagger, helmet, CORS, throttler, pino, global validation pipe, global exception filter
- [ ] **server:** health check endpoint `GET /health`
- [ ] **web + admin:** Next.js setup with Tailwind, shadcn/ui, TanStack Query provider, Axios instance, Zustand store
- [ ] **all repos:** ESLint, Prettier, Husky, lint-staged, README with setup steps
- [ ] **all repos:** GitHub Actions CI: lint + type-check + test on every PR

### Scenarios
- A new developer can clone, run `docker compose up` and `npm run dev`, and everything starts.
- A missing or wrong env variable makes the app fail at startup with a clear message.
- The API rejects requests from origins that aren't allowed (CORS).
- Too many requests return `429`.
- An unknown route returns a clean JSON `404`, not a stack trace.

### Testing
- **Unit:** config validation, exception filter
- **Integration:** DB connection, migrations run on an empty DB
- **E2E:** `GET /health` returns `200`
- **CI:** pipeline fails if lint, types, or tests fail

### Done when
- All three repos run locally from the README alone.
- CI is green on the main branch.
- Swagger opens at `/docs`.

tickets.title: [Auth] Authentication & multi-tenant access
tickets.body:
**Side:** All · **Phase:** M1 Setup & Auth · **Priority:** High · **Type:** Feature

### Summary
Login for the super-admin (platform) and for shop users (owner, manager, operator). Every token carries `tenantId` and `role`, so every request is automatically limited to that shop's data.

### What we'll use, and why
| Area | Tool | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| Tokens | @nestjs/jwt + @nestjs/passport + passport-jwt | Access token (15 min) + refresh token (7 days) |
| Passwords | argon2 | Password hashing |
| Validation | Zod (nestjs-zod) | Login and signup body validation |
| Roles | Guards + `@Roles()` decorator | `super_admin`, `owner`, `manager`, `operator` |
| Tenant scope | `@CurrentTenant()` decorator + tenant guard | Injects `tenantId` from the token into every query |
| Rate limit | @nestjs/throttler | Brute-force protection on login |
| Frontend | Axios interceptor | Attach token, auto-refresh on `401`, retry the request |
| Frontend | Next.js middleware | Protect routes, redirect to `/login` |
| Frontend | Zustand | Logged-in user, role, tenant info |
| Frontend | React Hook Form + Zod + shadcn Form | Login form |

### Database
- `users`: id, tenant_id (null for super_admin), name, phone (unique), email, password_hash, role, is_active, last_login_at
- `refresh_tokens`: id, user_id, token_hash, device info, expires_at, revoked_at
- `auth_logs`: user_id, tenant_id, action (login, logout, failed, refresh), ip, created_at

### API endpoints
- `POST /auth/login` (phone or email + password)
- `POST /auth/refresh`
- `POST /auth/logout` and `POST /auth/logout-all`
- `GET /auth/me`
- `POST /auth/change-password`
- `POST /auth/forgot-password` and `POST /auth/reset-password` (OTP)

### Token storage
- **Access token:** in memory (Zustand), not localStorage
- **Refresh token:** `httpOnly`, `secure`, `sameSite` cookie
- **Refresh rotation:** each refresh issues a new token and revokes the old one. Reusing an old token logs out all sessions.

### Tasks
- [ ] **server:** users, refresh_tokens, auth_logs tables + migration
- [ ] **server:** login, refresh, logout, me, change-password, forgot/reset password
- [ ] **server:** JWT strategy, `RolesGuard`, `TenantGuard`, `@CurrentUser()`, `@CurrentTenant()`
- [ ] **server:** throttle login (5 attempts per minute per IP + phone)
- [ ] **server:** block login for suspended tenants and inactive users
- [ ] **server:** seed one super-admin and one demo tenant with an owner
- [ ] **web + admin:** login page, Axios interceptor with refresh queue, middleware route protection
- [ ] **web + admin:** logout, "session expired" handling, role-based menu
- [ ] **admin:** only `super_admin` can log in to the admin panel

### Scenarios
**Login**
- Super-admin logs in → token has no tenantId, can open the admin panel
- Shop owner logs in → token has their tenantId and role `owner`
- Manager/operator logs in → limited menu based on role
- Wrong password → `401`, generic message "Invalid credentials" (don't reveal whether the phone exists)
- Unknown phone/email → same generic `401`
- Inactive user → `403` "Account disabled"
- Suspended tenant → `403` "Shop suspended, contact support"
- 6th failed attempt within a minute → `429`
- Empty, invalid, or very long fields → `400` with field errors

**Tokens and sessions**
- Access token expires → frontend refreshes silently, and the user notices nothing
- Several API calls fail with `401` at the same time → only **one** refresh request is sent, the rest wait and retry
- Refresh token expired or revoked → redirect to login with "Session expired"
- Old refresh token reused → all sessions of that user revoked
- Logout → refresh token revoked, cookie cleared
- Logout all devices → every session ends
- Login on two devices → both work independently

**Multi-tenant and roles**
- Shop A user requests shop B data by changing an ID → `404` (never shows B's data)
- Tampered JWT (changed tenantId or role) → `401`
- Operator calls an owner-only endpoint → `403`
- Shop user opens the admin panel → redirected or `403`
- Super-admin can view any tenant, but every action is logged

**Password**
- Change password with the wrong current password → `400`
- After a password change or reset → all other sessions revoked
- Reset OTP expired or used twice → rejected

### Testing
- **Unit:** password hashing/verify, token creation, guards, decorators
- **Integration:** login flow with a real test DB, refresh rotation, revocation
- **API E2E (supertest):** every scenario above
- **Security:** brute force (throttle), JWT tampering, expired token, wrong signature, `alg: none`, SQL injection in login fields, no password hashes in any response
- **Multi-tenant isolation:** an automated test that creates two tenants and checks shop A can't read or write shop B data
- **Frontend unit/component (Vitest + RTL):** login form validation, error messages
- **Frontend E2E (Playwright):** login → dashboard, token expiry → silent refresh, logout, protected route redirect
- **Manual:** mobile view of the login page, slow network, double-clicking the login button

### Done when
- All scenarios above pass in automated tests.
- No tenant can access another tenant's data.
- Tokens refresh without the user noticing.
- Every login, logout, and failed attempt appears in `auth_logs`.

tickets.title: [Backend] Tenants & multi-tenant data isolation
tickets.body:
**Side:** Backend · **Phase:** M1 Setup & Auth · **Priority:** High · **Type:** Feature

### Summary
Make tenant isolation automatic so no developer can accidentally leak one shop's data to another. Every business table carries `tenant_id`, and every query is scoped by it without the developer having to remember.

### What we'll use, and why
| Area | Tool | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| ORM | Drizzle ORM | Shared `tenantScoped()` query helper and base columns |
| Request context | nestjs-cls (AsyncLocalStorage) | Holds the current `tenantId` for the whole request |
| Database | PostgreSQL Row-Level Security (RLS) | Second safety layer: the DB itself blocks cross-tenant rows |
| Guards | `TenantGuard` + `@CurrentTenant()` | Reads `tenantId` from the JWT, rejects requests without it |
| Testing | Jest + supertest + test DB | Automated isolation tests |

### Database
- `tenants`: id, name, slug, owner_name, phone, email, address, city, logo_url, status (active / suspended / trial), plan, created_at, deleted_at
- Base columns for every business table: `id`, `tenant_id` (FK, NOT NULL), `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `deleted_at`
- Composite indexes starting with `tenant_id` (e.g. `(tenant_id, created_at)`)
- Unique constraints are per tenant, e.g. `UNIQUE (tenant_id, phone)` on traders
- RLS policy: `tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant_id')::uuid`, set at the start of each request transaction

### Tasks
- [ ] Create `tenants` table and base column helper for Drizzle schemas
- [ ] Request context: put `tenantId`, `userId`, `role` in CLS after JWT validation
- [ ] Repository/query helper that always adds `WHERE tenant_id = :tenantId` and sets `tenant_id` on insert
- [ ] Enable RLS on business tables and set `app.tenant_id` per request transaction
- [ ] Super-admin bypass: explicit `withTenant(tenantId)` call, always written to the audit log
- [ ] Reject any request body that tries to send its own `tenant_id` (ignored or `400`)
- [ ] Lint rule or code-review checklist: no raw queries on business tables without the helper
- [ ] Document the pattern in the server README

### Scenarios
**Normal use**
- Owner of shop A lists traders → only shop A traders returned
- Creating a record → `tenant_id` set from the token, never from the request body
- Same trader name or phone in shop A and shop B → both allowed

**Attacks and mistakes**
- Shop A user opens `/traders/<id of shop B trader>` → `404`
- Shop A user updates or deletes a shop B record by ID → `404`, nothing changes
- Request body contains `tenant_id` of another shop → ignored, record saved under the user's own tenant
- Developer forgets the helper in a raw query → RLS still returns zero rows from other tenants
- Token without `tenantId` calls a shop endpoint → `403`

**Tenant status**
- Suspended tenant → all shop endpoints return `403`, data stays safe
- Soft-deleted tenant → users can't log in, data kept for recovery

### Testing
- **Unit:** query helper adds tenant filter, insert sets tenant_id
- **Integration:** RLS policies block cross-tenant reads/writes on a real Postgres
- **API E2E:** two seeded tenants; every CRUD endpoint tested for cross-tenant read, update, delete
- **Security:** ID guessing, body tampering, missing tenant in token
- **Performance:** list queries use the `(tenant_id, …)` index (check with `EXPLAIN`)

### Done when
- Every business table has `tenant_id` + RLS enabled.
- Automated isolation test suite runs in CI and passes.
- Pattern documented so new modules follow it by default.

tickets.title: [Backend] Roles & permissions (RBAC) per tenant
tickets.body:
**Side:** Backend · **Phase:** M1 Setup & Auth · **Priority:** High · **Type:** Feature

### Summary
Control what each user can do. Platform level: `super_admin`. Inside each shop: `owner`, `manager`, `operator`. Permissions are checked on the server; the frontend only hides buttons.

### What we'll use, and why
| Area | Tool | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| Guards | NestJS `RolesGuard` + `PermissionsGuard` | Check role/permission on each endpoint |
| Decorators | `@Roles()`, `@Permissions()` | Declare access on controllers |
| Frontend | Zustand + a `can()` helper | Hide menu items and buttons the user can't use |

### Default permission matrix
- **super_admin:** manage tenants, plans, platform reports; no daily shop entries
- **owner:** everything inside own shop, including staff, settings, delete, reports
- **manager:** traders, rates, purchases, sales, payments, reports; no staff or settings
- **operator:** create purchases, sales, payments, view rates; no edit after the day closes, no delete, no reports

### Tasks
- [ ] Define roles and permission constants in one shared file
- [ ] `RolesGuard` / `PermissionsGuard`, applied globally with `@Public()` for open routes
- [ ] Return the user's permissions from `GET /auth/me`
- [ ] Frontend `can('purchase.delete')` helper for menu and buttons
- [ ] Owner can't remove their own owner role (at least one owner per shop)

### Scenarios
- Operator tries to delete a purchase → `403`
- Manager opens staff management → `403` on API, menu item hidden
- Owner changes a manager to operator → new permissions apply on the next token refresh
- Last owner tries to downgrade themselves → `400`
- Super-admin calls a shop-only endpoint without choosing a tenant → `403`
- Hidden button bypassed with a direct API call → server still returns `403`

### Testing
- **Unit:** guards with each role, permission matrix
- **API E2E:** one test per role per protected endpoint group
- **Frontend component:** menu and buttons render per role
- **Security:** role tampering in token, direct API calls

### Done when
- Every endpoint has an explicit role/permission or `@Public()`.
- Role tests run in CI.

tickets.title: [Backend] Audit log & soft delete
tickets.body:
**Side:** Backend · **Phase:** M1 Setup & Auth · **Priority:** Medium · **Type:** Feature

### Summary
Record who changed what and when, and never hard-delete business data. Mandi disputes happen; the audit log is the proof.

### What we'll use, and why
| Area | Tool | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| Interceptor | NestJS interceptor | Captures create/update/delete actions automatically |
| Database | `audit_logs` table (JSONB) | Stores before/after values |
| ORM | Drizzle | `deleted_at` filter on all reads |

### Database
- `audit_logs`: id, tenant_id, user_id, entity, entity_id, action (create/update/delete/restore), before (jsonb), after (jsonb), ip, user_agent, created_at
- All business tables: `deleted_at` (nullable)

### Tasks
- [ ] Audit interceptor/service called from all write operations
- [ ] Soft delete in the query helper; default reads exclude deleted rows
- [ ] Restore endpoint for owners
- [ ] Audit log list API with filters (user, entity, date) for owner and super-admin
- [ ] Never log passwords, tokens, or OTPs

### Scenarios
- Operator edits a purchase weight → log shows old and new weight, user, time
- Owner deletes a trader → trader hidden, still in DB, restorable
- Deleted trader's old purchases still show the trader name in reports
- Shop A owner can't see shop B audit logs
- Login with a password → password never appears in any log

### Testing
- **Unit:** diff builder, sensitive field masking
- **Integration:** write → audit row created in the same transaction
- **API E2E:** soft delete, restore, audit filters, tenant isolation

### Done when
- Every write on business tables produces an audit row.
- No hard deletes in business modules.

tickets.title: [Admin] Super-admin panel layout & navigation
tickets.body:

### Summary
Base layout for the platform owner's admin panel: sidebar, header, protected routes, and pages that later screens plug into.

### What we'll use, and why

| Framework | Next.js App Router | Route groups `(auth)` and `(dashboard)` |

tickets.title: [Web] Shop panel layout, navigation & role-based menu
tickets.body:
**Side:** Web · **Phase:** M1 Setup & Auth · **Priority:** High · **Type:** Feature

### Summary
Base layout for the shop owner/staff panel used every day in the mandi. Shows the shop name and logo, and a menu based on the user's role.

### What we'll use, and why
| Area | Tool | Used for |

| Permissions | `can()` helper | Role-based menu |

### Tasks
- [ ] Layout with shop name/logo in the header (from tenant settings)
- [ ] Menu: Dashboard, Rates, Purchases, Sales, Traders, Commodities, Ledger, Payments, Reports, Staff, Settings

- **E2E (Playwright):** login as owner and operator, compare visible menu, try a blocked URL

tickets.title: [Admin] Shop (tenant) management: create, suspend, activate
tickets.body:
**Side:** Admin · **Phase:** M2 Masters · **Priority:** High · **Type:** Feature

### Summary
Super-admin creates a new shop, which creates the tenant and its owner account in one step, and can suspend or reactivate any shop.

### What we'll use, and why
| Area | Tool | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| Backend | NestJS `TenantsModule` (super_admin only) | Tenant CRUD + status changes |
| Transactions | Drizzle transaction | Tenant + owner user + default settings created together |
| Table | TanStack Table + shared DataTable | Shops list with search, filter, pagination |
| Forms | React Hook Form + Zod | Create/edit shop form |
| URL state | nuqs | Search and filters kept in the URL |

### API endpoints
- `GET /admin/tenants` (search, status filter, pagination)
- `POST /admin/tenants` (shop + owner details)
- `GET /admin/tenants/:id`, `PATCH /admin/tenants/:id`
- `POST /admin/tenants/:id/suspend`, `POST /admin/tenants/:id/activate`

### Tasks
- [ ] **server:** endpoints above, all `super_admin` only, all audited
- [ ] **server:** create tenant + owner + default settings in one transaction
- [ ] **server:** suspending a shop revokes all its users' refresh tokens
- [ ] **admin:** shops list page, create/edit form, shop detail page, suspend/activate with confirmation
- [ ] **admin:** show owner's temporary password once, or send an invite link

### Scenarios
- Create shop with valid data → tenant, owner, and settings created; owner can log in
- Owner phone already used → `409`, nothing created (transaction rolled back)
- Suspend shop → its users are logged out within one token lifetime and can't log back in
- Activate shop → users can log in again
- Search by shop name, owner, phone, city
- Non-super-admin calls these endpoints → `403`

### Testing
- **Unit:** create-tenant service rollback
- **API E2E:** create, duplicate phone, suspend, activate, role checks
- **Frontend E2E:** create shop → log in as the new owner

### Done when
- Super-admin can onboard a shop end to end without touching the database.

tickets.title: [Backend] Shop onboarding & staff invitations
tickets.body:
**Side:** Backend · **Phase:** M2 Masters · **Priority:** Medium · **Type:** Feature

### Summary
Shop owners add their staff (managers, operators). Staff join through an invite link or a temporary password, always inside the owner's tenant.

### What we'll use, and why
| Area | Tool | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| Tokens | Signed one-time invite token (hashed in DB) | Secure invite links |
| Messaging | SMS / WhatsApp provider (to be chosen) | Send invite link or OTP |
| Queue (later) | BullMQ | Send messages in the background |

### Database
- `invitations`: id, tenant_id, phone, role, token_hash, expires_at, accepted_at, invited_by

### API endpoints
- `POST /staff/invitations`, `GET /staff/invitations`, `DELETE /staff/invitations/:id`
- `POST /auth/accept-invite` (token + name + password)

### Tasks
- [ ] Invite, list, cancel invitations (owner only)
- [ ] Accept invite: create user in the inviting tenant with the invited role
- [ ] Invite expires after 48 hours, single use
- [ ] Optional: owner sets a temporary password instead; user must change it on first login

### Scenarios
- Owner invites an operator → operator accepts → can log in to that shop only
- Invite link used twice → second use rejected
- Expired invite → rejected with a clear message
- Phone already registered in another shop → `409` (one user belongs to one shop)
- Manager tries to invite → `403`
- Cancelled invite → link stops working

### Testing
- **Unit:** token creation/verification, expiry
- **API E2E:** full invite flow, reuse, expiry, role checks, tenant isolation
- **Security:** token guessing, tampered role in the accept request

### Done when
- Owner can add staff without super-admin help.

tickets.title: [Web] Staff management (users & roles)

tickets.title: [All] Shop settings (profile, parchi header, commission, units)
tickets.body:
**Side:** All · **Phase:** M2 Masters · **Priority:** Medium · **Type:** Feature

### Summary
Each shop configures its own details used across the app: name, logo, address on the parchi, default commission and charges, units, and bill number prefix.

### What we'll use, and why
| Area | Tool | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| Backend | `tenant_settings` table | One row per tenant |
| Uploads | S3-compatible storage (e.g. Cloudflare R2) + react-dropzone | Shop logo upload |
| Forms | React Hook Form + Zod | Settings form with sections |

### Database
- `tenant_settings`: tenant_id, display_name, logo_url, address, phones, parchi_footer, default_commission_pct, market_fee_pct, labour_per_bag, default_unit (kg/maund), maund_kg (default 40), bill_prefix, financial_year_start, language

### API endpoints
- `GET /settings`, `PATCH /settings` (owner only)
- `POST /settings/logo` (image upload)

### Tasks
- [ ] **server:** settings table, defaults created with the tenant, get/update endpoints
- [ ] **server:** logo upload with type/size validation (png/jpg, ≤ 1 MB)
- [ ] **web:** settings page with sections: Shop profile, Parchi, Charges & commission, Units, Numbering
- [ ] **web:** live parchi header preview

### Scenarios
- Owner changes commission % → new purchases use it; old ones keep their saved value
- Owner uploads a 5 MB file or a PDF as logo → rejected with a clear message
- Manager or operator opens settings → 403
- Maund set to 40 kg → weight conversions everywhere use 40

### Testing
- **Unit:** settings validation, defaults
- **API E2E:** update, upload, role checks, tenant isolation
- **E2E:** change settings → see them on a new parchi

### Done when
- Settings saved per shop and used by purchases, sales, and printing.

tickets.title: [Web] Reusable DataTable component (web + admin)
tickets.body:
**Side:** Web · **Phase:** M2 Masters · **Priority:** High · **Type:** Feature

### Summary
One table component used by every list screen: server-side pagination, sorting, search, filters, column visibility, and export.

### What we'll use, and why
| Area | Tool | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| Table | TanStack Table | Headless table logic |
| UI | shadcn/ui Table, DropdownMenu, Popover | Look and feel |
| URL state | nuqs | Page, sort, filters in the URL so links are shareable |
| Data | TanStack Query (`keepPreviousData`) | Smooth paging |
| Export | SheetJS (xlsx) | Export current view to Excel |
| Large lists | TanStack Virtual (optional) | Very long tables |

### Tasks
- [ ] Server-side pagination, sorting, global search with debounce
- [ ] Filter bar: date range, select, status
- [ ] Column visibility toggle, remembered per user (localStorage)
- [ ] Row actions menu, bulk select
- [ ] Empty, loading (skeleton), and error states
- [ ] Export to Excel button
- [ ] Shared API contract: `?page=&limit=&sort=&q=&filters` → `{ data, meta: { total, page, limit } }`

### Scenarios
- Change page, sort, or filter → URL updates; refresh keeps the same view
- Search typing → only one request after typing stops
- No results → friendly empty state
- API error → error state with retry button
- 10,000 rows on the server → table stays fast (paged)

### Testing
- **Component (Vitest + RTL):** sorting, paging, filters, empty/error states
- **E2E:** filters persist after refresh
- **Performance:** large dataset paging

### Done when
- Traders list uses it as the first real consumer.

tickets.title: [Backend] Traders module (kissan, beopari, arhti)
tickets.body:
**Side:** Backend · **Phase:** M2 Masters · **Priority:** High · **Type:** Feature

### Summary
Manage everyone the shop deals with: farmers (kissan) who sell, buyers (beopari) who buy, and other commission agents (arhti). Each trader belongs to one shop.

### What we'll use, and why
| Area | Tool | Used for |

tickets.title: [Backend] Commission & charges calculation
tickets.body:
**Side:** Backend · **Phase:** M4 Purchases & Sales · **Priority:** High · **Type:** Feature

### Summary
One shared calculator for gross amount, commission, market fee, labour, and other deductions, used by purchases, sales, previews, and reports so totals always match.

### What we'll use, and why
| Area | Tool | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| Shared package | TypeScript module used by server and web | Same calculation everywhere |
| Numbers | decimal.js | Exact decimal maths |

### Money and weight rules
- Money stored as `numeric(14,2)`; weights as `numeric(12,3)` in kg
- All maths with decimal.js on the frontend and in services, never JS floats
- Rates, commission %, and charges are **copied onto the record** when saved, so later setting changes don't alter history

### Tasks
- [ ] `calculateTransaction({ weightKg, rate, rateUnit, bags, charges })` → gross, each deduction, net
- [ ] Charge sources in order: commodity override → shop default → manual override on the entry
- [ ] Rounding rule agreed with the client (e.g. to nearest rupee) and applied once at the end
- [ ] Return a line-by-line breakdown for the parchi

### Scenarios
- 1,000 kg at Rs 4,000 per maund (40 kg) → gross Rs 100,000
- Commission 2% + market fee 0.5% + labour Rs 20/bag × 10 bags → correct net
- Zero weight or negative rate → validation error
- Commodity override present → override used instead of shop default
- Same input on server and web → identical result

### Testing
- **Unit:** table-driven tests with real mandi examples from the client, rounding edge cases
- **Contract:** server and web produce the same numbers for the same fixtures

### Done when
- Calculator covered by tests with client-verified examples.

tickets.title: [Backend] Purchases API (buying from kissan)
tickets.body:
**Side:** Backend · **Phase:** M4 Purchases & Sales · **Priority:** High · **Type:** Feature

### Summary
Record goods bought from a farmer: commodity, bags, weight, rate, deductions, and net payable. Saving a purchase also writes the ledger entries in the same transaction.

### What we'll use, and why
| Area | Tool | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| Backend | NestJS `PurchasesModule` + Drizzle transactions | Purchase + items + ledger in one atomic save |
| Calculator | Shared commission & charges module | Totals |
| Validation | Zod (shared) | Same rules on web and server |
| Idempotency | `Idempotency-Key` header | No duplicates on double-click or retry |

### Database
- `purchases`: id, tenant_id, bill_no, trader_id, purchase_date, gross_amount, total_deductions, net_amount, paid_amount, status (draft/posted/cancelled), notes, created_by
- `purchase_items`: id, tenant_id, purchase_id, commodity_id, bags, weight_kg, rate, rate_unit, amount
- `purchase_charges`: id, tenant_id, purchase_id, type (commission/market_fee/labour/other), basis, value, amount

### API endpoints
- `POST /purchases` (with `Idempotency-Key`)
- `GET /purchases` (date range, trader, commodity, status)
- `GET /purchases/:id`, `PATCH /purchases/:id` (before day close), `POST /purchases/:id/cancel`

### Money and weight rules
- Money stored as `numeric(14,2)`; weights as `numeric(12,3)` in kg
- All maths with decimal.js on the frontend and in services, never JS floats
- Rates, commission %, and charges are **copied onto the record** when saved, so later setting changes don't alter history

### Tasks
- [ ] Schema and migrations
- [ ] Create: validate → calculate → assign bill number → insert purchase, items, charges, ledger entries in one transaction
- [ ] Edit allowed only before the day is closed (owner can always edit, audited); edit reverses and re-posts ledger entries
- [ ] Cancel instead of delete: reversing ledger entries, bill number kept
- [ ] Optional immediate payment on the same save

### Scenarios
- Save purchase → ledger shows the kissan credited with the net amount
- Double-click Save → only one purchase created (idempotency)
- DB error halfway → nothing saved (no purchase without ledger)
- Edit weight after saving → totals and ledger corrected, audit shows old values
- Cancel purchase → ledger reversed, bill marked cancelled, number not reused
- Inactive trader or commodity → `400`
- Operator edits after the day is closed → `403`
- Shop A can't read or cancel shop B purchases

### Testing
- **Unit:** service totals, edit/cancel ledger reversal
- **Integration:** transaction rollback on failure
- **API E2E:** create, idempotency, edit, cancel, filters, permissions
- **Multi-tenant:** cross-tenant access blocked
- **Concurrency:** two operators saving at the same time get different bill numbers

### Done when
- Purchase totals always equal the ledger effect.

**Side:** Backend · **Phase:** M5 Ledger & Payments · **Priority:** High · **Type:** Feature

### What we'll use, and why
| Area | Tool | Used for |

- `GET /ledger/balances` (all traders: receivable / payable)

- Money stored as `numeric(14,2)`; weights as `numeric(12,3)` in kg
- All maths with decimal.js on the frontend and in services, never JS floats
- Rates, commission %, and charges are **copied onto the record** when saved, so later setting changes don't alter history

- [ ] Ledger service used by purchases, sales, payments (never written directly by controllers)
- [ ] Running balance and opening balance for any date range
- [ ] Manual adjustment entries with mandatory reason, owner only
- [ ] Reconciliation check job: sum of documents = sum of ledger (alerts on mismatch)

- Cancelled purchase → reversal entry, balance back to before

tickets.title: [DevOps] Deployment, backups & monitoring
tickets.body:
**Side:** All · **Phase:** M6 Reports & Launch · **Priority:** High · **Type:** DevOps

### Summary
Production-ready hosting for server, web, and admin with staging, automatic database backups, error tracking, and uptime alerts.

### What we'll use, and why
| Area | Tool | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| Hosting | To be decided (e.g. VPS with Docker, or managed platform) | Run server, web, admin |
| Database | Managed PostgreSQL or Postgres on VPS | Production DB |
| CI/CD | GitHub Actions | Deploy on merge to main (staging) and on release tag (prod) |
| Errors | Sentry | Error tracking for server and frontends |
| Uptime | Uptime monitor (e.g. UptimeRobot) | Alerts when down |
| Backups | Daily `pg_dump` to object storage + point-in-time recovery if available | Data safety |

### Tasks
- [ ] Staging and production environments with separate databases and secrets
- [ ] Automatic migrations on deploy
- [ ] HTTPS, domain, CORS for production origins
- [ ] Daily backups kept 30 days; **test a restore**
- [ ] Sentry and uptime alerts to the team

### Scenarios
- Merge to main → staging updates automatically
- Failed migration → deploy stops, previous version keeps running
- Restore yesterday's backup into a fresh DB → app works with that data
- Server error → Sentry alert within minutes

### Testing
- **Manual:** restore drill, rollback drill
- **Smoke:** health checks after every deploy

### Done when
- Backup restore tested; staging and production running.

tickets.title: [Testing] Security review & load testing before launch
tickets.body:
**Side:** All · **Phase:** M6 Reports & Launch · **Priority:** High · **Type:** Testing

### Summary
Final check before real shops use the system: security review focused on multi-tenant isolation, plus load testing of busy mandi hours.

### What we'll use, and why
| Area | Tool | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| Load testing | k6 | Simulate many operators saving at once |
| Security | OWASP ZAP baseline scan + manual review | Common web vulnerabilities |
| Dependencies | npm audit / Dependabot | Vulnerable packages |

### Tasks
- [ ] Run the full multi-tenant isolation suite against staging
- [ ] OWASP Top 10 checklist: auth, access control, injection, XSS, CSRF, rate limits, secrets
- [ ] Load test: 50 shops × 5 operators saving purchases for 10 minutes
- [ ] Check slow queries and add indexes
- [ ] Fix all high/critical findings before launch

### Scenarios
- Peak load → p95 save time under 500 ms, no duplicate bill numbers, no errors
- Scanner finds no high-severity issues
- Cross-tenant attempts all blocked

### Testing
- **Load:** k6 scripts in the repo
- **Security:** ZAP report attached to this ticket

### Done when
- Report attached; no open high or critical issues.
